sections.title: Searching for Axion Dark Matter via Superconductor-Spin Hybrid Magnetometers
sections.published: Submission date shown as 2026-10-20; exact UTC timestamp not available from sources checked.
sections.abstract: The authors use a ferrite-spin sensor with SQUID readout to search for axion dark matter and report terrestrial limits on axion–electron coupling across 5–60 kHz.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report sub-100 aT/√Hz sensitivity at tens of kHz and 95% Bayesian constraints on axion–electron coupling from a ten-run search; they report no surviving candidate signal.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; ferrite spin sensor, superconducting quantum-interference-device readout, and ten measurement runs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The APS Physical Review Letters accepted-paper listing corroborates journal acceptance; the paper links a concrete sensor demonstration to a new frequency band for axion searches.
sections.unique_caveat: The constraint interpretation uses a standard axion dark-matter halo model; the projected improvement of more than four orders of magnitude from future sensor arrays is a forecast, not a demonstrated sensitivity.

sections.title: The Electron-Recoil Response Tail and the LZ High-Energy Event Background
sections.published: Submission date shown as 2026-10-19; exact UTC timestamp not available from sources checked.
sections.abstract: The authors show that response distributions matching the released LZ model’s central characteristics can imply electron-recoil tail probabilities differing by more than five orders of magnitude.
sections.claimed_result: Using a released detector-response configuration, the authors construct counterexample distributions with the same mean, variance, skewness and near-matching central quantiles but widely different extreme-tail leakage probabilities.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; response-model reconstruction, simulation, and constructed distribution families.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors released reproducibility code and derived data through GitHub and Zenodo, and the claim received independent technical discussion; both make the central argument checkable beyond the abstract.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly say their constructed families are not physical response models or a confidence interval, and they do not claim that the LZ collaboration’s internal calibration is wrong or revise the reported event significance.

sections.title: Parallel Omnidirectional Atom Rearrangement with Dynamic Holograms
sections.published: Submission date shown as 2026-10-19; exact UTC timestamp not available from sources checked.
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate rapid, parallel three-dimensional rearrangement of ytterbium atoms with dynamic holograms and assemble a 2,078-site kagome array at 99.0% mean filling.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that sub-millisecond SLM updates can increase transport speed despite reduced tolerable step sizes, and demonstrate parallel transport between array layers using a warm-start weighted Gerchberg–Saxton algorithm.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; ytterbium optical-tweezer arrays, survival/heating measurements, and hologram-control tests.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work is cross-listed across atomic physics, quantum gases and quantum physics, reports a quantitative large-array demonstration, and provides an implementation repository on GitHub.
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstrated filling and transport performance are specific to the authors’ apparatus and protocols; movement remains limited by heating and atom loss, especially over repeated steps.

sections.title: P-ONE-1: the first detector line of the Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment
sections.published: Submission date shown as 2026-10-20; exact UTC timestamp not available from sources checked.
sections.abstract: The P-ONE collaboration reports the design, construction and system-level tests of its first deep-sea neutrino-telescope line, prepared for deployment in Ocean Networks Canada’s NEPTUNE observatory.
sections.claimed_result: The collaboration reports successful construction and multi-site system validation of P-ONE-1, the first line of a planned high-energy neutrino telescope in the Northeast Pacific.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; detector integration and in-air/in-water engineering validation, not an astrophysical neutrino observation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: This is a concrete detector-infrastructure milestone with reported in-air and in-water validation, cross-listed in instrumentation and astrophysical methods.
sections.unique_caveat: The line is described as prepared for deployment; the paper does not report neutrino detections or demonstrate the completed telescope’s eventual sensitivity.

sections.title: Supermassive Black Hole Winds in X-rays -- SUBWAYS. VI. Interplay between the soft X-ray excess and ultra-fast outflows
sections.published: Submission date shown as 2026-10-17; exact UTC timestamp not available from sources checked.
sections.abstract: The authors analyze simultaneous or near-simultaneous UV, optical and X-ray observations of 21 active galactic nuclei to compare soft-excess, ultra-fast-outflow and warm-absorber models.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that a two-corona model describes the broadband data, while 9 of 21 objects favor a hybrid model including relativistic reflection; four of seven UFO-host observations favor that hybrid description.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; 21 AGN studied with XMM-Newton, NuSTAR and Hubble Space Telescope data.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper is accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics and combines XMM-Newton, NuSTAR and Hubble data in a multi-instrument study.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors caution that the sample is small and some trends depend on spectral parameters and instrumental response; the optical-depth/UFO-velocity anticorrelation is tentative.

sections.title: Numerical shock broadening and supernova neutrino conversion: implications for DUNE
sections.published: Submission date shown as 2026-10-19; exact UTC timestamp not available from sources checked.
sections.abstract: The authors compare stored and narrowly reconstructed shock fronts in three-dimensional supernova models and find that numerical shock broadening can change calculated neutrino flavor conversion.
sections.claimed_result: In the authors’ reconstructions, the ray-averaged MSW crossing probability rises by 0.44–0.76 in selected configurations; a separate parameterized-shock calculation changes the modeled 40-kiloton argon charged-current count by −4.4%.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; Garching three-dimensional blue-supergiant models, ray propagation, and a separate parameterized-shock calculation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The study tests six public three-dimensional explosion models, reports quantified changes across twelve configurations, and provides code according to the arXiv comments.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that folding the reconstructed three-dimensional fronts with a consistent emission model remains to be done; the event-count estimate is not a prediction from that full calculation.

sections.title: Polynomial-Time Classical Simulation of BosonSampling under Any Constant-Fraction Photon Loss
sections.published: Submission date shown as 2026-10-19; exact UTC timestamp not available from sources checked.
sections.abstract: The authors give a polynomial-time approximate classical sampler for two standard lossy BosonSampling models when a constant fraction of photons survives.
sections.claimed_result: For Haar-random interferometers, the authors prove polynomial-time sampling within total-variation error ε with probability at least 1−δ for fixed surviving fractions under fixed-loss and uniform-transmission-loss models.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical; algorithmic complexity analysis for specified random-interferometer and photon-loss models.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result gives an explicit complexity guarantee in the linear-survival regime, extending the stated range of previously provable efficient simulation and directly addressing a central assumption in photonic quantum-advantage proposals.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is conditional on the stated interferometer and loss models and does not establish efficient simulation for every photonic circuit or experimental task.

sections.title: Charmed baryon decays at BESIII
sections.published: Submission date shown as 2026-10-20; exact UTC timestamp not available from sources checked.
sections.abstract: This conference proceeding summarizes recent BESIII measurements and observations of charmed-baryon production, polarization and decay channels using its 6.4 fb⁻¹ data sample.
sections.claimed_result: The author summarizes first observations of Λc⁺→ne⁺νe and Λc⁺→nπ⁺η using deep-learning techniques, alongside other recent BESIII results.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; BESIII e⁺e⁻ collision data at 4.60–4.95 GeV, summarized in a conference proceeding.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The proceeding reports several new decay-channel observations and a polarization measurement from BESIII’s large Λc-pair data sample; it is explicitly identified as an ICHEP 2026 contribution.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a short proceedings summary of multiple analyses, not a single combined measurement; detailed uncertainties and analysis-specific limitations are not available in the abstract.
